questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 2 AM and 3 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
The time is between **2 AM** and **3 AM**. Let the time be **2:M**.

Position of the **hour hand** at 2:M (relative to 12 o'clock):

Initial position at 2 o'clock = 2 × 30° = 60°

Movement in M minutes = M × 0.5°

Total angle = 60° + 0.5M

Position of the **minute hand** at 2:M (relative to 12 o'clock):

Total angle = 6M

For the hands to **overlap**:

6M = 60 + 0.5M

6M − 0.5M = 60

5.5M = 60

M = 60 ÷ 5.5 = 120/11

M = 10.9090... minutes

Rounding to the **nearest minute**, we get M ≈ 11 minutes.

The time (approximately) is **2:11 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The time at which the hands of a clock overlap between **H** and **H+1** o'clock is given by the formula:

M = (60)/(11) times H

Here, **H = 2** (for the time between 2 AM and 3 AM).

So, M = (60/11) × 2

M = 120/11

M = 10.909...

M ≈ 11 minutes.

Therefore, the hands overlap at approximately **2:11 AM**.

The correct answer is **2:11**.

questions.question: Which constitutional body audits the accounts of the Union and states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Comptroller and Auditor General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)** is an independent authority established under **Article 148** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The CAG serves as the head of the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department** and acts as the **guardian of the public purse**, ensuring financial accountability of the executive to the Parliament.
 
• According to **Article 149**, the CAG audits all expenditure from the **Consolidated Fund of India**, the **Consolidated Fund of each State**, and the **Consolidated Fund of each Union Territory** having a Legislative Assembly.
 
• The CAG also audits all expenditure from the **Contingency Fund of India** and the **Public Account of India**, as well as the contingency fund and public account of each state.
 
• Under **Article 151**, the audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the **President**, who causes them to be laid before each **House of Parliament**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission**:

 
 
• Established under **Article 280** of the Constitution, it is a quasi-judicial body that recommends the distribution of **tax proceeds** between the Union and the States and the principles governing **grants-in-aid**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• Replacing the Planning Commission on **January 1, 2015**, it is a **non-constitutional** and **non-statutory** body serving as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**:
 
 
• A constitutional body established under **Articles 315 to 323** of Part XIV, responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to the **services of the Union**.

questions.question: Which type of emergency has never been proclaimed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Emergency Provisions** are contained in **Part XVIII** of the **Constitution of India**, spanning from **Article 352 to Article 360**.
 
• **Article 360** empowers the **President** to proclaim a **Financial Emergency** if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• Although India faced a severe **economic crisis** in **1991** related to the **balance of payments**, a **Financial Emergency** was not declared.
 
• To date, the **Government of India** has **never** invoked **Article 360**; therefore, a **Financial Emergency** has never been proclaimed in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**:

 
 
• It is proclaimed on grounds of **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**.
 
• In India, it has been proclaimed **three times**: in **1962** (Indo-China war), **1971** (Indo-Pak war), and **1975** (internal disturbance).
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** replaced the term 'internal disturbance' with '**armed rebellion**'.
 
 
 
• **President's Rule (Article 356)**:
 
 
• Also known as **State Emergency** or **Constitutional Emergency**, it is imposed when a State Government cannot be carried on in accordance with the **Constitution**.
 
• This has been proclaimed **numerous times** (more than 100 instances) across various states since **1950**.
 
• **Punjab** was the first state where **President's Rule** was imposed in **1951**.
 
 
 
• **Approval and Duration**:
 
 
• A **National Emergency** must be approved by **Parliament** within **one month**, whereas **President's Rule** and **Financial Emergency** must be approved within **two months**.
 
• Once approved, **Financial Emergency** continues indefinitely until it is revoked by the **President**.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Advocate General of a State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 165** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Governor** of each state has the authority to appoint the **Advocate General** for the State.
 
• To be eligible for the appointment, the person must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of a High Court**, which requires being a **citizen of India** and having held a **judicial office** for ten years or served as an **advocate** in a High Court for at least ten years.
 
• The **Advocate General** serves as the **highest law officer** of the state government, providing legal advice and representing the state in legal matters assigned by the **Governor**.
 
• The Constitution does not provide a fixed tenure for the **Advocate General**; the official holds office during the **pleasure of the Governor** and receives remuneration as determined by the **Governor**.
 
• Conventionally, the **Advocate General** resigns when the **Council of Ministers** (government) resigns or is replaced, as they are appointed on its advice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• The **President of India** is responsible for appointing the **Attorney General of India** under **Article 76**, who is the corresponding highest law officer at the central level.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**:
 
 
• The **Governor** exercises the power of appointment based on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers**, which is headed by the **Chief Minister**.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**:
 
 
• While the **State Legislature** does not appoint the **Advocate General**, the official has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the **Legislative Assembly** and **Legislative Council** (under **Article 177**) without the **right to vote**.

questions.question: What is the frequency range of sound that can be heard by the human ear?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human ear is sensitive to sound waves within a specific frequency range, typically spanning from **20 Hz** to **20,000 Hz** (or 20 kHz).
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the number of vibrations or cycles per second, and its **SI unit** is the **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal mechanical waves** that require a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel; they cannot propagate through a **vacuum**.
 
• The human ear is most sensitive to frequencies between **2,000 Hz** and **5,000 Hz**, which is the range where most human speech and communication occur.
 
• The anatomy of the ear, specifically the **tympanic membrane** (eardrum) and the **cochlea**, is biologically tuned to process vibrations within this specific audible spectrum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasonic Sound**:

 
 
• Refers to sounds with frequencies below **20 Hz**, which are too low for the human ear to perceive.
 
• These waves are produced by large-scale phenomena such as **earthquakes**, **volcanic eruptions**, and **ocean waves**.
 
• Certain animals like **elephants**, **hippos**, and **whales** utilize infrasound for long-distance communication.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasonic Sound**:
 
 
• Refers to sounds with frequencies exceeding **20,000 Hz**, which are beyond the upper limit of human hearing.
 
• Used extensively in medical **ultrasonography** (sonography) for imaging internal organs and in industrial applications like non-destructive testing.
 
• Animals such as **bats**, **dolphins**, and **porpoises** use ultrasound for **echolocation** to navigate and hunt in the dark or underwater.
 
 
 
• **Hearing Variations**:
 
 
• The upper limit of hearing typically decreases with age, a physiological phenomenon known as **presbycusis**.
 
• Children can often hear frequencies slightly above **20,000 Hz**, whereas elderly adults may have a restricted range ending at **12,000 Hz** or lower.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest contributor to urban PM2.5 in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vehicle exhaust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM2.5** refers to atmospheric particulate matter with a diameter of less than **2.5 micrometers**, which is small enough to enter the bloodstream and cause severe cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.
 
• In urban India, the **transportation sector** (vehicle exhaust) is consistently identified as the **largest primary contributor** to PM2.5 levels. Source apportionment studies by **IIT Kanpur** and the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** indicate that vehicles contribute between **28% and 47%** of the total PM2.5 load in major cities like **Delhi** and **Mumbai**.
 
• **Vehicle exhaust** is particularly critical because it releases pollutants at the **ground level**, leading to higher human exposure compared to industrial stacks which disperse pollutants at greater heights.
 
• While **Construction dust** is a significant source of coarser particles (PM10), its relative contribution to the finer **PM2.5** fraction is typically lower than that of combustion-related sources.
 
• **Industrial emissions** are major contributors in specific industrial zones, but on a city-wide average for residential and commercial **urban areas**, the sheer volume of **diesel and petrol vehicles** makes exhaust the dominant source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial emissions**:

 
 
• These involve pollutants from **power plants** and manufacturing units, primarily contributing **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** and nitrogen oxides, which can form **secondary PM2.5** in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Construction dust**:
 
 
• Comprises crustal materials like **silica** and cement particles; while it adds to the **dust load**, it is generally easier to mitigate through **water sprinkling** and green barriers compared to chemical exhausts.
 
 
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**:
 
 
• Launched in **2019**, this initiative aims for a **20% to 30% reduction** in PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by **2024** across 131 non-attainment cities in India.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Stage VI (BS-VI)**:
 
 
• India skipped **BS-V** and transitioned directly to **BS-VI** norms on **April 1, 2020**, to drastically reduce particulate matter and nitrogen oxide emissions from **new vehicles**.

questions.question: Which of the following meteorological factors can reduce Air Quality Index (AQI) temporarily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rain** or **precipitation** acts as a natural air purifier through a process known as **wet deposition**. It is the most effective meteorological mechanism for the temporary removal of pollutants from the atmosphere.
 
• As raindrops fall, they collide with and capture suspended **particulate matter** (including **PM10** and **PM2.5**) through mechanical processes such as **impaction**, **diffusion**, and **interception**. This is technically referred to as **below-cloud scavenging** or **washout**.
 
• Rain also facilitates the removal of soluble gaseous pollutants like **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** and **nitrogen dioxide (NO2)** by dissolving them into water droplets, which then reach the ground.
 
• The physical removal of these contaminants leads to a rapid decrease in the concentration of pollutants in the immediate breathing zone, resulting in a significantly lower **Air Quality Index (AQI)** reading.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature Inversion**:

• The primary mechanism through which these substances work is by binding to **androgen receptors** within muscle cells. This activation stimulates **protein synthesis** and promotes **nitrogen retention** in the muscles, which are critical components for **hypertrophy** (increased muscle size).
 
• Athletes and bodybuilders misuse these drugs to achieve a rate of muscle growth and physical strength that far exceeds what is naturally attainable through diet and exercise alone. This allows for a more significant **lean body mass** and enhanced physical appearance. Hence, the statement **Build muscle mass** is correct.
 
• Beyond simple growth, anabolic steroids help in the production of **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)** and promote the expansion of **satellite cells**, which are essential for repairing and thickening muscle fibers after high-intensity training sessions.

• **Enhance flexibility:** Steroids do not improve flexibility; in fact, excessive muscle bulk and the tightening of tendons can sometimes lead to a **decreased range of motion**.
 
• **Reduce fatigue:** Although steroids allow for faster recovery between workouts by reducing **muscle damage** and inflammation, they are not classified as stimulants or fatigue-reducing agents like **caffeine** or **amphetamines**.
 
 
 
• **Health Risks of Misuse:**
 
 
• Cardiovascular issues such as **hypertension**, increased **LDL cholesterol**, and risk of heart attacks.

HCF and LCM Property

questions.question: sqrt{108900 + sqrt{12321}} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the individual square roots using simple visual observation:

⇒ **√12321** = 111 (using the standard palindromic pattern where 111² = 12321)

⇒ **√108900** = 330 (since 33² = 1089 and the square root of two trailing zeros is one zero)

⇒ Substituting these values: √(330 + 111) = √441 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = √(√108900 + √12321)

**Calculation:**

First, calculate the value of the inner square roots:

⇒ Let x = √12321

⇒ x = 111

⇒ Let y = √108900

⇒ y = 330

Now, substitute the values of x and y back into the main expression:

⇒ Required value = √(y + x)

⇒ Required value = √(330 + 111)

⇒ Required value = √441

⇒ Required value = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Palindromic Numbers

For numbers consisting of digits that increase sequentially up to a peak and then decrease (e.g., 121, 12321, 1234321), the square root contains only 1s, where the count of 1s equals the peak digit. Thus, √12321 = 111.

Square Root of Numbers with Trailing Zeros

When finding the square root of a perfect square ending in an even number of zeros, the square root contains exactly half as many zeros at the end. For example, √108900 = √1089 × √100 = 33 × 10 = 330.

Simplification Hierarchy

In mathematical expressions involving nested radicals, always simplify the innermost operations first before proceeding outward to the main radical.

questions.question: There is a rectangular garden of 150 metres × 60 metres. A path of width 2 metres is build outside the garden. What is the area (in square metre) of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **area of a path** built **outside** a rectangle, use the formula:

**Area = 2w(L + B + 2w)**

Where **L** = 150 m, **B** = 60 m, and **w** = 2 m.

Area = 2 × 2 × (150 + 60 + 2 × 2) = 4 × (210 + 4) = 4 × 214 = 856 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 856 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fd783123297f3b0a51bd9c104f82131538cfd3fb1e0b17411b1fa1cb57934c7.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ **Length of garden (L)** = 150 m

⇒ **Breadth of garden (B)** = 60 m

⇒ **Width of path (w)** = 2 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the path is outside, **Outer Length** = 150 + 2 + 2 = 154 m

⇒ **Outer Breadth** = 60 + 2 + 2 = 64 m

⇒ **Area of Path** = (Outer Length × Outer Breadth) − (Inner Length × Inner Breadth)

⇒ Area = (154 × 64) − (150 × 60)

⇒ Area = 9856 − 9000

⇒ Area = 856 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 856 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Path Inside a Rectangle

If the path is built inside the rectangular garden, the formula becomes Area = 2w(L + B − 2w).

Central Cross Paths

Area of two paths crossing each other at the center of a rectangle is given by Area = w(L + B − w).

Circular Path

The area of a circular path around a circle with radius 'r' and width 'w' is π((r+w)² − r²) = πw(2r + w).

questions.question: A new student having weight 40 kg join a class of 39 students. The average weight of the class reduces by 0.5 kg. What is the new average weight (in kg) of the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**New Average** = **New Weight** + (**Initial Students** × **Reduction**)

⇒ **New Average** = 40 + (39 × 0.5)

⇒ **New Average** = 40 + 19.5

⇒ **New Average** = 59.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial students = 39

Weight of new student = 40 kg

Reduction in average = 0.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfa1fd2e4eb2e14079e48b4432412a528666ba5b956043d7ede0fedba1defc28.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **initial average weight** of the 39 students be **x** kg.

⇒ Total weight of 39 students = 39 × x = 39x

⇒ Total weight of 40 students (including the new student) = 39x + 40

⇒ New average weight = **x − 0.5**

⇒ **New Average** = (Total weight of 40 students) ÷ 40

⇒ x − 0.5 = (39x + 40) ÷ 40

⇒ 40 × (x − 0.5) = 39x + 40

⇒ 40x − 20 = 39x + 40

⇒ 40x − 39x = 40 + 20

⇒ x = 60 kg (Old Average)

⇒ **New Average weight** = 60 − 0.5 = 59.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their average is always zero. New member weight − Old average = Total members × Change in average.

Weighted Average Formula

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the individual average/value.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

When a new person joins, New Value = New Average + Initial Number × (Change in Average). If the average decreases, the change is considered positive in this specific adjustment format.

questions.question: Average of some numbers is 'p'. 22 is the smallest number among these numbers. Which of the following statement will be always correct? I. p = 35. II. 50 will be the largest number among these numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Average (p)** of a set of numbers must always satisfy the condition: **Smallest Number ≤ p ≤ Largest Number**.

Given the **Smallest number** is 22, the **Average (p)** can be any value greater than or equal to 22, and the **Largest number** can be any value greater than or equal to 22.

Statement I claims **p** is exactly 35, which is not mandatory.

Statement II claims the **Largest number** is exactly 50, which is also not mandatory.

Since both are specific cases and not universal rules, neither is always correct.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Smallest number** = 22, **Average** = p.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7f4d3e9419b059fcdee305552a3e8ca9529af2ea8cb1c7bc3aebd64e5cad1aa.png] 

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 23}. Here, **Average (p)** = 22.5 and **Largest** = 23. (Both I and II are False)

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 48}. Here, **Average (p)** = 35 and **Largest** = 48. (Statement II is False)

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 22, 106}. Here, **Average (p)** = 50 and **Largest** = 106. (Statement I is False)

⇒ Since we can find instances where these statements do not hold, they are not **always correct**.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Range Property of Average

The average of any data set must lie strictly between (or equal to) the minimum and maximum values of the set: **xₘᵢₙ ≤ Average ≤ xₘₐₓ**.

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their **Arithmetic Mean** is always zero: **Σ(xᵢ − p) = 0**.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every term in a set, the new average will be **p ± k**.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 9 and their Highest Common Factor is 3. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **ratio** of two numbers is a : b and their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is H, then the numbers are (a × H) and (b × H).

Given **Ratio** = 7 : 9 and **HCF** = 3.

Numbers = (7 × 3) and (9 × 3) = 21 and 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 21, 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Ratio** of numbers = 7 : 9 and their **HCF** = 3.

**Formula Used:** Number = Ratio Unit × HCF

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82a841be72a593dc21c2b5eb546565027455b8499b6c55ec9d1555ae25862a54.png] 

⇒ Let the two numbers be **7x** and **9x**.

⇒ The **HCF** of 7x and 9x is **x** (since 7 and 9 are **co-prime** numbers).

⇒ According to the question, **HCF = 3**.

⇒ Therefore, **x = 3**.

⇒ First number = 7 × 3 = **21**.

⇒ Second number = 9 × 3 = **27**.

**∴ The correct answer is 21, 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**. Formula: **HCF × LCM = n₁ × n₂**.

LCM from HCF and Ratio

If the ratio of two numbers is **x : y** and their **HCF** is **H**, then their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is given by **LCM = x × y × H**.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor** is **1**. In a simplified ratio a : b, a and b are always co-prime.

questions.question: An interval of 8 hours 20 minutes is wrongly estimated as 8 hours 40 minutes. What is the error percentage?
questions.solution:

Convert values to a common unit: **Actual time** = 500 min and **Estimated time** = 520 min.

Absolute **Error** = 520 − 500 = 20 min.

**Error percentage** = (Error ÷ Actual Value) × 100.

Error % = (20 ÷ 500) × 100 = 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual time interval = 8 hr 20 min

Estimated time interval = 8 hr 40 min

**Formula Used:**

Error Percentage = (Absolute Error ÷ Actual Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df548a0d32df6a4eff21b4ffc17db8de298fa956c02dc56585e443c2238bfc3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual time in minutes = (8 × 60) + 20 = 480 + 20 = 500 min

⇒ Estimated time in minutes = (8 × 60) + 40 = 480 + 40 = 520 min

⇒ Absolute Error = 520 − 500 = 20 min

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Absolute Error

Relative Error

Percentage Change

The formula for **percentage increase** or **decrease** is always calculated on the **original (base) value**: (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100.

questions.question: A pipe can empty 1/5 part of a tank in 36 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) will it empty the complete tank?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In fraction-based problems, the **Total Work** is represented by the **denominator**.

If **1 unit** (out of 5) takes **36 min** to empty,

Then **5 units** (complete tank) will take 36 × 5 = **180 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part of the tank emptied = **1/5**

Time taken to empty this part = **36 minutes**

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = (Time Taken) ÷ (Part Emptied)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3190c0f592c52d548db79d11302a1cfd76e70923bb427e16a37429240f659051.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **total capacity** of the tank be 1 unit.

⇒ Time taken to empty 1/5 part = 36 min

⇒ Time taken to empty 1 unit = 36 ÷ (1/5)

⇒ Total Time = 36 × 5

⇒ Total Time = 180 min

**∴ The correct answer is 180 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Rule

questions.question: Speed of a train is 54 km/hr. This train crosses a platform in 18 seconds. Length of the platform is double of the length of the train. What is the length (in metres) of the train?

Ratio of **Train Length** : **Platform Length** = 1 : 2.

Total distance = 15 m/s × 18 sec = 270 m.

1 unit (Train Length) = 270 ÷ 3 = 90 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 m.**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 54 × (5/18) = 15 m/s

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
He needs to finish this task by evening.

options.text: The task needs to finished by him by evening.
The task needs to be finished by him by evening.
The task needs to be finish by him by evening.
The task needs to finish by him by evening.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The task needs to be finished by him by evening.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Active Voice** with the structure: **Subject (He)** + **Main Verb (needs)** + **Infinitive (to finish)** + **Object (this task)** + **Time Phrase (by evening)**.

• To convert a sentence with an **infinitive (to + V1)** into **Passive Voice**, the structure of the infinitive must change from **to + V1** to **to + be + V3 (Past Participle)**.

• The **Object** of the active sentence (**this task**) becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence. In the options provided, **The task** is used as the new subject.

• The **Subject** of the active sentence (**He**) changes to its **Objective Case** (**him**) and is placed after the preposition **by**.

• The main verb **needs** remains in the **Simple Present Tense** to agree with the new singular subject **The task**.

• Combining these rules, **to finish** becomes **to be finished**, resulting in the correct passive construction.

 **Additional Information__**

• Analysis of incorrect options:

• **Option 1**: **The task needs to finished** is grammatically incorrect because it omits the mandatory auxiliary verb **be** required for the passive infinitive form.

• **Option 3**: **The task needs to be finish** is incorrect because it uses the **Base Form (V1)** instead of the **Past Participle (V3)** form **finished** after **be**.

• **Option 4**: **The task needs to finish** uses the **Active Infinitive**, which implies the task itself is performing the action of finishing, which is logically and grammatically flawed in this context.

• Common **Passive Voice** Transformations:

• **Active:** Subject + Verb + to + V1 + Object.

• **Passive:** Object + Verb + to + be + V3 + by + Subject.

</ul

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**keeps reverting to her bad habits**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence contains a grammatical error known as **redundancy** or **pleonasm**. This occurs when a word is used that repeats the meaning already contained within another word in the same phrase.

• The verb **revert** is defined as returning to a former state, practice, habit, or condition. The prefix **re-** in Latin-based words typically signifies **back** or **again**.

• Because the concept of moving **back** is already inherent in the definition of **revert**, adding the word **back** immediately after it is unnecessary and considered incorrect in **formal English**.

• Option 1 provides the correct improvement by removing the redundant adverb **back** and maintaining the prepositional phrase **to her bad habits**, making the sentence concise and grammatically sound.

• Options 2 and 3 are incorrect because **reverting backward** remains redundant, and **reverting forth** is logically contradictory, as **forth** implies forward movement which opposes the meaning of **revert**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Common Redundancies**:

• **Return back**: To return means to come or go back; therefore, **back** is extra.

• **Reply back**: To reply is to answer back, making **back** redundant.

• **Added bonus**: A bonus is something added, making the word **added** unnecessary.

• **End result**: A result occurs at the end, making **end** redundant.

• **Etymology of Revert**:

• Originates from the Latin word **revertere**, where **re-** means back and **vertere** means to turn.

• In legal contexts, it refers to **reversion**, where property returns to the original owner or their heirs after a specific period or event.

• In **software engineering**, to **revert** a commit means to undo changes and return the code to a **previous state**.
